source: Kuwaiti landscaping company price lists: hadeiq.com (2026 indicative), hdaiqkwit.com, hadeqtak.com (Feb 2026), landscapingcompanykuwait.com
quote: الثيل الصناعي بين 3.5 و8 دنانير للمتر المربع، والطبيعي مع تجهيز التربة بين 4 و9
note: Natural turf (roll-out sod, usually Bermuda/Paspalum) supplied and laid in Kuwait: hadeiq.com 4–9 KD/m² with soil preparation (2026 indicative); hdaiqkwit.com natural grass installation from 4 KD/m²; hadeqtak.com 1.5–2 (economy), 2–3 (mid) and 3–4.5 KD/m² (premium) including supply and basic installation; landscapingcompanykuwait.com from 2.5 KD/m². Value 4 KD/m² includes levelling and a thin layer of sweet soil/fertiliser; heavy soil replacement or imported varieties go to 9. Irrigation is separate (irrigation:sprinkler_m2).

source: wikikuwait.com (Feb 2026, Kuwaiti installers by pile height); janaalbustan.com (Kuwait supply + installation rates); hadeiq.com 2026
quote: سعر الثيل الصناعي سماكة 40 ملليمتر 3.5 دينار كويتي.
note: Kuwaiti supply+install prices: Al-Masa 20–26 mm 2.5, 30 mm 2.65, 36 mm 3.0, 40 mm 3.5, 50 mm 4.0 KD/m²; Al-Bahja 3.5; Al-Naseem 2.5 any thickness (wikikuwait, Feb 2026). Classified ads (4Sale/OpenSooq, Sep 2026) advertise from 3 KD/m². janaalbustan: supply 2.5–4 (20–26 mm), 4–6 (30–36 mm), 6–8 KD/m² (40 mm); installation 1–1.5, ground preparation + installation 2–3, full service 7–12 KD/m². hadeiq 3.5–8 KD/m². Value 5 KD/m² for a 35–40 mm turf with base levelling and compacted sand; 2.5 is cheap turf laid on existing ground. One outlier (tansiqq.com, Nov 2025) quotes 15–25 KD/m² and is excluded.

source: Bottom-up from Al Jahra Nursery Kuwait online prices (shrubs, ground cover, soil mix, compost) + planting allowance
note: No Kuwaiti per-m² rate for planting beds was found, so this is built up from Al Jahra Nursery (Kuwait) 2026 prices: shrubs Leucophyllum 70 cm 3.0, Carissa 70 cm 3.5, Clerodendrum 110 cm 4.0 KD; ground cover Alternanthera 40 cm 1.5, Duranta 40 cm 1.0 KD; Agricultural Soil Mix 20 kg 1.0 KD; Organic Compost 40 L 3.0 KD; Peat Moss 340 L 12.0 KD. Per m²: 2 shrubs (~6.5) + 2–3 ground-cover plants (~3) + ~10 cm soil improvement (~2–3 with bulk sweet soil; more with bagged mix) + labour (~1) ≈ 12 KD. Low 6 for sparse planting on existing soil; high 20 for dense planting with bagged soil. Drip irrigation is separate (irrigation:drip_m2).

source: Kuwaiti retail pebble prices: Plant N Pot (20 kg bag) and Al Jahra Nursery; layer depth and membrane are assumptions
note: No Kuwaiti per-m² rate found. Kuwaiti retail: Plant N Pot white garden stones 5.5 KD per 20 kg bag; Al Jahra Nursery Snow White Pebbles 3.0 KD per bag (weight not stated; 20 kg assumed). UAE cross-check: Falaj Garden natural white pebbles AED 32 per 20 kg (≈2.5 KD). A 4 cm layer of 20–40 mm pebbles weighs ≈65 kg/m² ≈ 3.2 bags → 9.6–17.6 KD, plus weed membrane and labour ≈1 KD/m² (assumption) → 11 (8–19) KD/m². Bulk-delivered gravel (by the truck) is cheaper than bagged retail; the low end allows for that.

quote: تبدأ الأسعار من 7 دنانير وقد تصل إلى 14 دينارًا للمتر
note: Interlocking concrete pavers (البلاط المتداخل) in Kuwait: installation only 2.5–6 KD/m²; supply + installation 7–14 KD/m² (hadeqtak 2026; local makers Al-Watania, Al-Ittihad, Al-Kuwaiti, Al-Messila). hadeiq.com lists interlock at 4–9 KD/m². Value 8 KD/m² for standard 6–8 cm pavers on a compacted sand bed; kerbstones are extra. High end for patterned/coloured or natural-stone-look units.

source: Al Jahra Nursery Kuwait (Albizia lebbeck 300 cm, Cassia glauca 300 cm); UAE nursery Conocarpus 2–2.5 m prices (fop.ae, growhub.ae, plantsworld.ae) + planting allowance
note: Kuwait supply prices (Al Jahra Nursery, 2026): Albizia lebbeck 300 cm 15 KD; Cassia glauca 300 cm 5 KD; Bambar tree 350 cm 100 KD (specimen). Mashatel Kuwait: Conocarpus 80 cm in 17 cm pot 2.5 KD. UAE, low confidence: Conocarpus 2–2.5 m AED 130 (fop.ae 200–230 cm; growhub.ae) to AED 189 (plantsworld.ae), VAT included → /1.05 ×0.0836 ≈ 10–15 KD. Planting (pit, sweet soil, compost, stake, first watering) adds ~3–5 KD (assumption; Kuwaiti planting services on OpenSooq start at 5 KD per job). Value 18 KD for a 2–3 m tree supplied and planted; 8 for a cheap 2 m Conocarpus/Cassia, 30 for a larger Ficus nitida or Albizia. Note: Conocarpus roots damage drains and foundations; many Kuwaiti designers now avoid it near buildings.

source: Kuwaiti classifieds: sooq.in (Barhi tissue-culture palm, digging/transport/planting extra) and OpenSooq Kuwait (Barhi palm, Sep 2026)
quote: نخل برحي نسيجي نوعيه ممتازه ومنتج ب 130 دينار
note: Kuwait: a productive tissue-culture Barhi date palm 130 KD where it stands (sooq.in, Kuwait, late 2025); the same seller charges 12 KD for a Washingtonia in place or 17 KD with digging (شلع), transport and planting, i.e. +5 KD for a small palm. OpenSooq Kuwait (Sabah Al-Ahmad, 21 Sep 2026): Barhi palm 90 KD each, negotiable. Trunk height is not stated in either ad; a productive palm usually has a 1.5–3 m trunk. A 2–3 m-trunk date palm needs a crane/hiab truck, a large pit, sweet soil and bracing; ~20 KD is allowed for this (assumption) → 130 + 20 = 150 KD. Low = 90 + 5; high 200 (estimate for larger or Ikhlas/Sukkari palms). Ornamental Washingtonia 200 cm is 115 KD at Al Jahra Nursery for comparison.

source: Al Jahra Nursery Kuwait outdoor shrub prices; hdaiqkwit.com (Kuwait) seasonal shrub planting rate
note: Kuwait supply prices (Al Jahra Nursery, 2026): Leucophyllum frutescens 70 cm 3.0, Carissa grandiflora 70 cm 3.5, Clerodendrum splendens 110 cm 4.0, Duranta 40 cm 1.0, Buddleja saligna 3.0 KD. Planted rate: hdaiqkwit.com starts at 1.5 KD per seedling for planting seasonal shrubs/flowers ("1.5 د.ك للشتلة"). PAAF's Al-Omariya nursery sells seedlings at a subsidised 50 fils–1 KD (2022), about 10% of commercial value. Value 3.5 KD = a 60–100 cm shrub (~3 KD) + ~0.5 KD planting; low 1.5 for small seedlings; high 5 for 1 m+ flowering shrubs.

source: Dar Al Rawda Landscaping (Kuwait) irrigation price table: drip systems for 300 m² and 500 m² gardens
quote: ري بالتنقيط | حديقة 300م²: 550-750 دينار | حديقة 500م²: 850-1150 دينار
note: Dar Al Rawda (Kuwait): drip irrigation 550–750 KD for a 300 m² garden (1.8–2.5 KD/m²) and 850–1,150 KD for 500 m² (1.7–2.3 KD/m²); smart systems 850–1,800 KD. These whole-system prices include mains/laterals, emitters, valves and a basic controller. If irrigation:controller and irrigation:valve are counted separately, use ~1.7 KD/m². Material check (UAE Falaj Garden): 16 mm drip line with 30 cm emitters ≈ AED 180 per 400 m roll (≈0.04 KD/m of line), so most of the cost is labour, fittings, mains and valves. High 3.5 for small, fragmented beds.

source: Dar Al Rawda Landscaping (Kuwait) irrigation price table: sprinkler systems for 300 m² and 500 m² gardens
quote: ري بالرش عادي | حديقة 300م²: 450-650 دينار | حديقة 500م²: 700-950 دينار
note: Dar Al Rawda (Kuwait): basic sprinkler system 450–650 KD for 300 m² (1.5–2.2 KD/m²) and 700–950 KD for 500 m² (1.4–1.9 KD/m²). Component check (UAE Falaj Garden): pop-up sprinkler with 15VAN nozzle AED 45 per 5 (≈0.75 KD each). hadeiq.com quotes a whole automatic network at 150–500 KD per villa project; an OpenSooq Kuwait ad (Sep 2026) offers automatic irrigation installation from 100 KD.

source: Falaj Garden UAE bubbler price (component) + Kuwaiti install allowance
quote: Bubbler with Stick for Irrigation (13mm tube, Pack of 5): AED 22.50
note: No Kuwaiti price found; UAE component price used (low confidence): AED 22.50 per 5 bubblers on stakes, VAT assumed included → /1.05 ×0.0836 ≈ 0.36 KD each. A tree/palm bubbler point also needs ~3–5 m of 16 mm feeder line, a tee/adapter and labour, so ~2 KD installed (estimate, not sourced). Palms often get 2 bubblers or a ring of drippers. High 4 for adjustable pressure-compensating bubblers (Rain Bird/Hunter) on a riser.

source: Bab Al-Saif (BAS Kuwait) online prices: 1 HP water pump (Italy) and automatic pump control
quote: Water Pump 1 HP (Italy) - BAS Kuwait: 34.000 KWD
note: Kuwait retail: BAS Kuwait 1 HP water pump (Italy) 34.0 KD; automatic pump control 1100 W 7.45 KD; a 0.5 HP Dingqi pump is 9.95–11.95 KD. Pump + pressure control ≈ 41.5 KD; suction/delivery pipework from the tank, non-return valve, isolating valves, an outdoor socket/isolator and labour add ~20–25 KD (estimate) → 65 KD. Kuwaiti villas usually irrigate from the ground or roof tank (MEW water); bigger gardens use a dedicated irrigation tank. High 110 is an estimate for a branded multistage pump with a pressure vessel (not a sourced price).

source: hadeiq.com (Kuwait 2026 indicative) complete small-yard price; cross-checked by summing this file's rates
quote: حوش صغير كامل (40 – 60 م²) | للمشروع | ثيل ومظلة وري وإنارة | 600 – 1,500
note: Cross-check only. hadeiq.com: a complete small yard of 40–60 m² (grass, shade structure, irrigation and lighting) costs 600–1,500 KD → 10–37.5 KD/m² (pergola included). hdaiqkwit.com lists design/landscaping packages of 150 KD (≤50 m²), 250 KD (50–150 m²) and 400 KD (large villa garden), which look like design-and-basic-work fees, not full builds. Bottom-up for a typical villa garden of ~50% lawn/turf (4–5), 30% planting beds (12), 20% paving (8), irrigation (~2) and a few trees/palms ≈ 10–15 KD/m². Value 15 KD/m²; 8 for mostly turf + gravel; 35 with pergolas, lighting and specimen palms.

source: Abdul Salam & Al Mazrooei (Kuwait University), Acta Horticulturae 736 (2007): Kuwait ETo and date-palm ETc; Dar Al Rawda (Kuwait) lawn guidance
quote: The annual potential evapotranspiration (ETo) of Kuwait was estimated as 2883 mm.
note: Water-demand rule, not a price; basis is a placeholder. No KISR or PAAF figure for garden irrigation per m² was found online. Kuwait University study (43 years of agro-met data): annual ETo 2,883 mm; date-palm monthly ETc 74 mm (Jan) to 392 mm (June) ≈ 13 mm/day at the June peak. Warm-season turf (Bermuda/Paspalum) uses ~0.6–0.8 of ETo → ~8–10 mm/day in summer; with ~75–80% sprinkler efficiency that is ~10–13 L/m²/day (1 mm = 1 L/m²). Shrub beds on drip use less (~5–7 L/m²/day). Dar Al Rawda (Kuwait): «العشب يحتاج 4-6 لترات لكل متر مربع يومياً في الصيف», which looks like a well-managed minimum. Value 10 L/m²/day for lawn in July–August; 5 for drip-irrigated beds; 15 for lawn on sandy soil in peak heat.
